text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: redis-cache-prod - high blocked_clients (threshold 10) - page fired

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident INC-2026-4532 created and paged schedule 'oncall-sre' :bell:

sara_oncall: acked. I'm on it, ping me if anything customer-facing comes up.

alex_db: i'm jumping in. quick check: `redis-cli -h redis-prod-1 INFO clients | egrep \"blocked_clients|maxclients|connected_clients\"` returned:
```
# Clients
connected_clients:520
blocked_clients:62
maxclients:1024
```

alex_db: blocked_clients is high but not > maxclients. looks like a large number of clients are stuck waiting on sync/long commands (likely `BGREWRITEAOF` or slow Lua).

nina_sre: seeing high latency spikes on the cache layer in Datadog graphs (p95 > 300ms for 10m). correlates with a surge of write bursts from api-prod.

sara_oncall: any evictions or OOM events?

alex_db: checked `redis-cli -h redis-prod-1 MONITOR` for a minute — lots of `EVAL` and `ZINTERSTORE` calls with big input sizes. also a few `script kill` attempts in the logs. suspect a thundering herd of cron jobs + a new release that added an expensive cache priming routine.

james_support: Customer impact: support queue shows 4 high-priority customers reporting increased API latency and timeouts. triage/ES calls are being retried.

sara_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) remove the heavy cache priming by disabling the scheduled job 2) scale read replicas / add an extra redis node 3) enable read-only fallback for majority of clients

alex_db: doing step 1 now. patch to disable job rolled to api-prod: `kubectl -n prod delete cronjob cache-prime` (rolled back the cron for now).

ops-bot: Deploy bot: rollout started for deployment api-primer-v2 -> replicas decreased from 3 to 0 in prod (probe).

nina_sre: disabling that job dropped new blocking commands. however existing blocked_clients still high — we should try `CLIENT UNBLOCK` for obvious stuck connections and `CLIENT KILL TYPE normal` for older idle ones.

alex_db: running:`redis-cli -h redis-prod-1 CLIENT LIST | awk -F ' ' '{print $1,$2,$3,$5}' | grep -E 'age=|addr=' | head -n 20` to identify candidates. then `CLIENT KILL addr <ip>:<port>` for the ones stuck > 300s.

sara_oncall: please coordinate kills carefully — some customers have long-running streams. annotate kills with reason.

alex_db: executed a targeted `CLIENT KILL` batch (60 connections). blocked_clients dropped from 62 -> 8, p95 latency back to ~45ms.

james_support: update to support: two of the four customers reported reduction in errors, one still seeing intermittent timeouts (they use pub/sub heavily), escalated to account team.

nina_sre: added temporary alert suppression for repeated blocked_clients pages (60m) so we don't flood oncalls while mitigation in progress — will remove after incident cleared.

sara_oncall: good call. i'm going to keep the page open until we confirm stable for 30m and then follow with a postmortem. next steps:
- identify offending release or job (rollback of cache-prime seems to have helped)
- add circuit breaker on heavy EVAL/ZINTERSTORE paths
- consider connection pooling on clients to avoid many short-lived connections
- add a dashboard that flags long-running client age > 120s and command type

alex_db: i'll own the postmortem and put mitigation notes in the runbook. initial blameless cause: expensive cache priming plus unexpected scale in write traffic => blocked clients and latency.

james_support: i'll update customers with a summary: temporary cache priming job caused increased cache load; we've disabled the job, killed stuck connections; engineering monitoring in place.

sara_oncall: handoff: @nina_sre will monitor for the next 2 hours, i'll be available on pager for followups.

nina_sre: monitoring. letting alarms re-enable in 30m. please create incident channel for postmortem notes?

sara_oncall: created channel #inc-redis-4532 (private) and added incident-bot, alex_db, nina_sre, james_support.

ops-bot: Incident channel created: #inc-redis-4532

sara_oncall: closing page for now, will reopen if blocked_clients > 20 for 15m. thanks everyone :heart:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-4532 acknowledged and transitioned to 'mitigation in progress'

alex_db: postmortem checklist items created and assigned to me (owner). will include timeline, root cause, mitigation, preventive actions and a targeted roll to limit EVAL/ZINTERSTORE sizes.

james_support: logging notes for customer comms. will draft a proactive post to affected accounts.

nina_sre: FYI: added a short-term runtime patch to our autoscaler to spin a warm spare Redis instance when avg blocked_clients > 20 for 5m. we'll evaluate if that should become permanent.

sara_oncall: nice. after postmortem let's add a playbook section: when blocked_clients spikes, first check for scheduled jobs, then targeted CLIENT KILL, then scale.

alex_db: thanks all. I'll push postmortem in 24h.

james_support: thumbs on comms drafts in #customer-comm once ready.

sara_oncall: incident closed (mitigated) at 1762956902. followups tracked in #inc-redis-4532 and our runbook. :white_check_mark:
